strengths: The practice board's outcome vocabulary is exactly right for a 13-year-old: 'Right first time', 'Got there in the end', 'Not yet' (php/lib/practice.php lines 71-73 and 943). It is growth-framed, plain, and never says 'wrong' or 'failed'. Do not let the dashboard's teacher vocabulary leak into it.

Session-scale progress already exists in the data model: MATHS_SCOREBOARD panel 1 is 'Questions this week' over a 7-day window (practice.php line 71), and every practice run stores attempted/correct/correct_after_retry with a date. The student view proposed below needs no new tables.

The personal best is self-referenced only: the gold star and dashed record line compare her to her own earlier runs, never to anyone else (practice.php lines 556-563, 588-595). That is the version of a 'badge' with the least downside, and it should stay.

No streaks, no leaderboards, nothing withheld for a missed day (README.md lines 232-239). For a student whose attendance will be variable, a loss-framed streak is the mechanic most likely to turn one missed day into a week away. Keep this.

Every session row carries a 'next_steps' string written by the tutor at the moment it knew most (dashboard.php line 353; live example: 'Resume at practice Q4 ... Then P4-P5'). This is the feed for a 'next' card; it only needs surfacing.

Charts are accessible by construction: each SVG has a <title> (practice.php line 569) and its numbers are repeated in a <details> table (lines 653-669); activity cards and date chips are ordinary links that work with JavaScript off (lines 1213, 1282).

The page cannot change a status. Reading is free, writing goes through evidence-checked tools. That keeps the page from becoming a chore or a notification surface, and it is the right call for the record; the student view should keep it.

'not played yet - give it a go' (practice.php line 1209) and the design page's 'One run is not a trend yet - play once more and the chart appears' (design/practice-ab/index.html line 665) are the right register: an invitation, not an instruction.

The exercise-book look (squared paper, Georgia, hand-rotated stamp, dashboard.php lines 20-36) reads as a school book rather than an admin console. Only the content of the stamp is the problem, not the style.

Pooled accuracy rather than mean-of-percentages (practice.php lines 363-370) means a short bad game cannot drag the headline number down disproportionately, which protects her from a misleadingly harsh number after a five-minute set.

findings.title: There is no student-facing view; every page is the tutor's audit record
findings.where: /home/user/education-study-tracker/php/lib/dashboard.php lines 157-431 (render_subject, section order at 393-428); /home/user/education-study-tracker/php/index.php lines 300-317 (routes /s/<slug> and /s/<slug>/practice only)
findings.problem: The only subject page is the audit dashboard. Its order (lines 393-428) is: red countdown, 'Spec conquered 23%', 'Lower-tier secure 17/55', 'Latest paper 148/240 ≈ grade below 4', an amber 'Due a retrieval check ... demote it to developing' flag, then practice tiles, six strand bars, 64 topic chips (100 for Spanish, 98 of them grey), 14 loose-end paragraphs, the resource list, papers, and week-by-week session narratives. Nothing on the first screen answers the two questions a student has: 'what do I do next?' and 'how did I do last time?'. Both answers are already in the database. The /s/spanish page is worse: 1% covered, no paper, and the chart she likes is not on it (see the separate finding).
findings.why_it_matters: The objective is that she engages. A page whose first screen is a deadline, a percentage that does not move, a grade below target and a warning gives an ADHD 13-year-old nothing to act on and several reasons to close the tab. COGA's 'Making Content Usable' asks for a clear purpose per page, minimal content, and the important thing first; this page is designed for the parent and tutor to read backwards, which is a different purpose.
findings.proposal: Add one route, /s/<slug>/today, rendered by a new render_student(Store $store, array $subject) in dashboard.php next to render_subject, using dash_shell so it inherits the look. One screen at 360x640, at most 120 words, phone-first, in this order: (1) Title: subject name; beneath it a muted small line 'Exam: 14 May 2027' - no day count, no red, no rotation. (2) NEXT TIME card, the largest element: the first one or two sentences of next_steps from the newest non-void row of $store->listSessions($slug, 5), followed by 'Then: <ref> <name>' for the first priority gap in the same order tracker_review_queue uses (reuse the store query behind it) with that topic's first resource from resourcesForTopic() as the one link on the card. Live example: 'Next time: resume practice Q4 and Q5 (biased dice). Then: G1 Conventions, terms, symmetry.' (3) LAST TIME card: the date of the newest practice run, then 'N questions · N right first time · N got there in the end' pooled over runs whose practice_run_date() equals that date via practice_stat_value(), then 'Moved up: P1, P2-P3' from changesForSession() on that day's sessions where the status rank rose. (4) THIS WEEK strip: the existing 'Questions this week' (7d) and 'Right first time' (last10) stat tiles rendered with practice_render_stat(), plus 'topics moved up this week' counted the same way over the last 7 days. (5) QUICK RECAP READY: the ageing secures (weeksSince(last_touched) >= 8) as up to four chips with one line 'you had these secure in June; a two-minute recap keeps them' - no 'demote'. (6) For Spanish, the 'Score trend' line panel from SPANISH_SCOREBOARD rendered with practice_render_line(); for maths, the 'How questions went' split panel limited to 6. (7) Footer: 'Full record for parents →' linking to /s/<slug>. Hide: the countdown number, Spec conquered %, Lower-tier secure, the latest-paper grade, strand bars, the topic chip wall, loose ends, resources list, papers & checks, session narratives, evidence strings, VOID rows. Feeds: sessions (date, next_steps, void_reason), topic_changes, practice_runs, topics (status, last_touched), resources. No schema change. Add one smoke-test line: contains "the student page renders a next card" "$page" 'class="next"'. Point the / index cards at /today for the student and keep /s/<slug> for the parent.
findings.evidence_needed: externalising executive function for ADHD (visible cues for initiation and planning); proximal sub-goals raising self-efficacy and persistence; COGA guideline on clear purpose and minimal content

findings.title: '252 days to the exam' in red pencil is the most salient thing on the page and offers no next step
findings.where: /home/user/education-study-tracker/php/lib/dashboard.php lines 34-36 (.countdown CSS: 2px #dc2626 border, #b91c1c text, rotate(2deg), 1.5rem number), 178-184 (day arithmetic), 367-370 (markup '252 days to the exam'), 394-397 (header placement)
findings.problem: The countdown is the largest number on the page, the only red element above the fold, and rotated like a stamp so the eye lands on it first. Today it reads 252 (maths) and 278 (Spanish). It states a distal deadline eight months away with no proximal target; the nearest thing she can act on - the December mock, the February tier decision - lives only in the skill appendix, not on the page. Red on a school page reads as 'wrong' or 'late'.
findings.why_it_matters: Time perception and future-oriented planning are the executive functions most affected in ADHD; a large distal number does not convert into today's action and can produce avoidance rather than urgency. Threat-framed cues raise anxiety without giving a controllable behaviour. The parent's stated goal is engagement, and the stamp is aimed at the parent's sense of pace, not hers.
findings.proposal: On the student view show only 'Exam: Thu 14 May 2027' in the muted small style (no count, no red, no rotation). On the full dashboard keep the stamp for the parent but consider counting to the next checkpoint instead of the exam: add a nullable next_checkpoint date and label to the subject row (a one-line migration step) so line 368 can read '97 days to the December mock', which is a target a session can visibly move towards. If no checkpoint is set, fall back to the exam date in neutral styling: change `.countdown` to border-color var(--line) and color var(--ink) unless a checkpoint is within 30 days.
findings.evidence_needed: time perception / temporal discounting deficits in ADHD; anxiety and avoidance under threat framing; proximal versus distal goals (goal-setting research)

findings.title: Progress is only visible at syllabus scale: two full sessions moved the headline from 22.9% to 22.9%
findings.problem: 'Spec conquered' is points/(64×3). On 2 Sep she did two 90-minute sessions, answered 20 questions with 19 right first time, and moved two topics from gap to developing; A4 also went secure→developing. Net points 44→44, so the headline stayed at 23%. Even a clean gap→developing move is 1/192 = 0.52%, which integer rounding hides half the time. The only session-scale figures on the page are the practice tiles, which sit below the countdown, three stat cards and the ageing flag.
findings.why_it_matters: If the page's summary number is insensitive to a whole day's work, the page teaches that effort does not register. Progress monitoring only motivates when the monitored quantity moves at the scale the person works at; for a 13-year-old with ADHD that scale is a session, a day, a week, not a two-year syllabus.
findings.proposal: Add a 'Since last time' strip above the stats row (and make it the centre of the student view): 'This week: 20 questions · 19 right first time · 2 topics moved up (P1, P2-P3)'. Questions and right-first-time come from the existing MATHS_SCOREBOARD stat panels ('Questions this week', window 7d; 'Right first time', last10) via practice_render_stat(); 'moved up' is a count over changesForSession() for sessions in the last 7 days where rank(to_status) > rank(from_status). Keep 'Spec conquered' for the parent but show it as a delta too: '23% (+1 this month)'. Note that blanks per session cannot be shown: 'blanks' is stored only on attempt papers, not on practice runs, so 'zero blanks' lives in the summary prose only - worth adding a blanks column to practice_runs later.
findings.evidence_needed: progress monitoring meta-analysis (frequency and proximity of monitoring to goal attainment); proximal sub-goals and self-efficacy; ADHD reward sensitivity to frequent, immediate reinforcement

findings.title: The no-streak, no-badge stance is right on penalties and comparison, over-broad on 'nudges'
findings.where: /home/user/education-study-tracker/README.md lines 232-239 ('There are deliberately no leaderboards, streaks, badges or nudges ... The gold star and the record line are the one concession ...'); lines 209-226 (the pinned Spanish chart)
findings.problem: Three different things are refused in one sentence. Streaks and leaderboards are loss-framed or comparative and punish exactly the day-to-day variability ADHD produces; refusing them is well founded. Badges have small and mixed effects in the gamification literature, and the gold star is already a badge in all but name - a good one, because it is self-referenced and earned by performance, not attendance. 'Nudges' covers both manipulative engagement loops and the supportive external cues (a visible next step, a reminder at a chosen time, immediate feedback) that are among the best-evidenced ADHD accommodations. The README currently bars the second kind along with the first, which is why the page has no 'next' card.
findings.why_it_matters: The objective is engagement. Extrinsic reward schemes can undermine intrinsic interest and streaks create obligation; but externalised cues that lower the cost of starting are not obligation, they are scaffolding. Treating them as the same thing leaves the student to self-initiate from a page that gives her nothing to initiate with.
findings.proposal: Rewrite README lines 232-239 to name the rule precisely. Replacement text: 'There are deliberately no leaderboards, streaks or attendance rewards, no cross-subject comparison and no per-keystroke telemetry. Nothing counts consecutive days or withholds anything for missing one: the board must never make a missed day cost more than a missed day. Rewards, where they exist, are for what she did (a personal best, a topic moved up), never for turning up. Cues are allowed: a visible next step, a personal best she can actually reach on a short game, and a reminder she has chosen herself. The gold star and the record line stay inside that rule because they compare her only with her own earlier runs.' Keep the gold star; fix its reachability (previous finding); add the next card (finding 5). If a reminder is ever added, make it opt-in, positive ('Q4 and Q5 are waiting'), and silent when missed.
findings.evidence_needed: gamification meta-analyses (badges/leaderboards/points effects on learning); undermining effect of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation; loss aversion and streak breakage; external cueing and reminders as ADHD accommodations

findings.problem: The page is read-only by design, and that is right for status. But it also offers no way to begin: the empty activity tiles invite her to play Flashcards and AI Conversation without linking to the app; the maths 'next' topic's Bitesize page is buried in the resources section; there is no link from the Spanish board to the Spanish app at all.
findings.why_it_matters: For ADHD the gap between 'I should' and 'I have started' is where sessions are lost. A page that is one tap from the activity turns the reinforcing chart into a doorway; a page that is a dead end sends her back to find the app somewhere else.
findings.proposal: Add an optional url to practice_sources (one migration step; tracker_set_scoreboard-style validation) and, when present, render the empty tile as '<a class="tile empty" href="…">' with the same text; render a small 'Play →' link on the played tiles too. Until the migration exists, fall back to a subject-wide resource with kind 'app'. In the student view the Next card carries the single link for the next topic (finding 5). Keep status write-only through the tools: the page should start things, not record them.
findings.evidence_needed: reducing initiation cost / friction for task start in ADHD; implementation intentions
